anti_overlap: Defers invocation/dismissal LIFO mechanics to fd-vedic-ritual-layered-invocation
Defers HUD strip glanceability mechanics to fd-lighthouse-keeper-logbook
decision_lens: When multiple entities co-occupy a tile, is the displayed priority order the same as the click-cycle order? Is that order encoded once or duplicated across systems?
distance_rationale: Chanoyu is a 500-year-old hospitality discipline focused on physical object placement and gesture sequencing, with no overlap to software UI, yet its utensil-priority and dismissal protocols map directly to selection-priority and tooltip-dismissal design.
expected_isomorphisms: Utensil priority on tray = entity priority on tile; temae sequence ambiguity resolution = click-cycle ordering; haiken inspection order = tooltip display order; placement-with-both-hands special case = polymorphic Selection variant handling.
focus: Chanoyu utensil placement priority, sequential hand-resolution, and dismissal ceremony as a structural model for sticky tooltip priority and selection cycling
name: fd-tea-ceremony-utensil-priority-protocol
persona: A tea-ceremony (chanoyu) procedural specialist analyzes the input system through the lens of dōgu placement protocol. On a tray, every utensil has an assigned position and a strict order of pickup-and-replace; when multiple utensils could be reached for the same gesture, the protocol specifies an unambiguous priority (chashaku before chasen, chawan handled with both hands). The 'temae' procedure resolves ambiguity in the same way the sticky right-click tooltip must resolve when multiple entities co-occupy a tile (an elf standing on a flora tile in front of a building). The closing 'haiken' inspection has a fixed sequence — the user examines utensils in defined order, not arbitrary order. The reviewer evaluates whether the priority order is explicit, stable, and surfaced consistently to the user.
review_areas: Whether the sticky right-click tooltip's 'all entities in priority order' uses the same priority function as left-click selection — duplication risks divergence
Whether priority among Selection variants (Elf > Building > Flora? or context-dependent?) is documented, stable, and resilient to new entity types being added

Whether the tooltip's stickiness (does not auto-dismiss) has a well-defined dismissal ceremony — what closes it: another right-click, Esc, click elsewhere, opening an overlay? — and whether that ceremony respects the modal stack
Whether the persistent HUD legend strip lists keybindings in a stable, glanceable priority order (most-frequently-used leftmost? grouped by mode?) consistent with how players scan it
Whether selection cycling (if the user repeatedly clicks the same tile) advances through entities in tooltip-display order, or in some other order — UI inconsistency would be a defect

Whether the polymorphic Selection's None variant has a defined visual representation (no tooltip? empty tooltip? default 'nothing here'?) — the absence of a selection should be as ceremonial as a present one

severity_examples.condition: Priority must be a single pure function consumed by both render and selection paths
severity_examples.scenario: Tooltip shows 'Elf, Building, Flora' but click-cycle goes 'Flora, Elf, Building' because two functions encode priority differently

severity_examples.condition: Tooltip dismissal must compose with stack push — opening any overlay should dismiss or hide tooltips
severity_examples.scenario: Sticky tooltip persists after pause menu opens, occluding part of the menu

severity_examples.condition: Priority extensibility should be data-driven, not hard-coded across three sites
severity_examples.scenario: Adding a new entity type (e.g. Animal) requires editing tooltip render, click-cycle, and selection match-arms separately, with no central registry

source_domain: Japanese tea ceremony (chanoyu) utensil placement and temae procedure
success_hints: Define a single fn entity_priority(tile) -> Vec<Entity> used by tooltip render, click-cycle, and any selection action
Specify tooltip dismissal triggers explicitly: list every event that closes a sticky tooltip and verify each fires the dismissal
For HUD legend: order keybindings by frequency-of-use, not alphabetically — match the player's scan pattern
task_context: Reviewing 9 locked decisions for native renderer input system in a Bevy 0.18 elven colony sim — modal stack, polymorphic Selection, sticky tooltip, persistent HUD, two-predicate gate, Direct overlay switching, hybrid camera gating
